hook.title: 2.6× faster than React. Don't trust us. Run it.
hook.lede: Ten frameworks, real Chromium, every arm on its own fast path. Pyreon builds 10,000 rows in 72.6 ms against React 19's 192.0. Every number on our board comes with its run count and the command that reproduces it.

sections.title: The numbers that survived.

stats.label: faster than React 19 creating 10,000 rows (72.6 vs 192.0 ms); 3.8× faster than Preact
stats.condition: final pass, two runs · Apple M3 Max · real Chromium · synthetic, author-run

stats.label: less JavaScript than React for the same keyed-table app (17.2 KB vs 69.6 KB gzip)
stats.condition: final pass, one run (sizes are deterministic)

stats.label: faster compiled server rendering than React 19 at 1,000 rows (109.9 vs 714.4 µs)
stats.condition: overnight run, one run · Apple M3 Max · synthetic, author-run

sections.note: Synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max. Absolute times are machine-dependent; compare ratios.

items.title: Clear rows: the outright row-board win
items.text: 130 µs vs Vue 3.6 Vapor (RC) 145 µs, 1.11–1.12×, with confidence intervals disjoint in both runs.

items.title: Tied for the lightest memory
items.text: Retained heap after the suite: Pyreon 3.08 MB and Preact 3.09 MB, ahead of Solid 3.16, Svelte 3.27, Vue 3 3.30 and React 3.50. Both runs.

items.title: Hydration that leads
items.text: On a 320-component app page Pyreon hydrates in 4.02 ms, ahead of React (4.15), Preact (4.30) and Vue (4.47). One run.

items.title: TodoMVC against React 19
items.text: Toggle 1,000 todos about 2.4× faster, clear 1,000 3–4× faster. One run.

items.title: Signals against Preact Signals
items.text: Effect propagation 2.04–2.13×, batching 1.94–1.95×, the computed diamond 1.30–1.31× on V8. Two runs.

items.title: Reproduce the row board
items.text: Strictly sequential, gated on a one-minute load below 4. You get 100 samples per cell from five page loads, framework order reshuffled every pass.
items.code:
git clone https://github.com/pyreon/pyreon && cd pyreon
bun install
cd examples/benchmark
bun bench-fair.ts --repeat 5 --wait-quiet 4

items.title: Read the verdict rules
items.text: A result is a win only when the confidence intervals are disjoint in both runs. Overlapping intervals mean "could not distinguish", never "equal". A close verdict needs two agreeing runs.

items.title: Check the rest
items.text: Every suite on the board, from SSR to the reactivity core, lists its own command on the benchmarks page.

sections.title: Eight bugs we found in our own benchmark.
text: Pyreon's authors wrote every harness, every competitor arm, and decide what counts as a win. Every judgement call in a setup like that leans toward the home team. So we went looking, and found eight measurement bugs. Each one was fixed, re-run and published, and each has a guard that stops it coming back.

sections.title: The eight, and the guard for each.

items.title: 1. Rivals on slow paths
items.text: Svelte and Vue arms ran on deep proxies and Octane was pinned eight patches behind. Guard: every arm on its framework's documented fast path.

items.title: 2. A 100 µs clock
items.text: Chromium clamps `performance.now()` on a non-isolated page. Guard: cross-origin isolated pages with a measured 5 µs quantum, and a batch instrument for tiny ops.

items.title: 3. A `String()` wrapper
items.text: It switched off Octane's compiler fast path. Guard: no presentation work a real user would not write; competitor arms are checked by compiling them.

items.title: 4. A V8 string cache
items.text: Its growth was billed to five arms' retained heap. Guard: every arm renders the raw `row.id`.

items.title: 5. `table-layout: auto`
items.text: Whole-table re-measures inflated a Pyreon partial-update lead; the published ~4.9× was withdrawn. Guard: `table-layout: fixed` plus a bimodality check.

items.title: 6. A busy machine
items.text: A hydration "tie" was measured at load 8.2. Guard: sequential runs gated on load below 4.

items.title: 7. A rival's upgrade
items.text: A clear-rows swing was mostly a competitor getting slower. Guard: split "Pyreon moved" from "competitor moved" before attributing a change.

items.title: 8. Pooled intervals
items.text: 100 samples from 5 page loads were treated as independent. Guard: a two-stage cluster bootstrap over page loads.

sections.text: Synthetic: these are synthetic micro- and scenario benchmarks. They do not predict the performance of your app.

sections.title: An independent venue, staged.
text: The only full answer to author bias is someone else's harness. A keyed Pyreon implementation for krausest/js-framework-benchmark is staged in the repo under `contrib/krausest/pyreon-keyed/`. Staged, not yet submitted.

sections.text: The board also lists where we are not first: Solid mounts a deep component tree 1.15–1.18× faster, Solid, Preact and Svelte ship smaller bundles, signal creation is about 5× slower than Preact Signals, and five row-board ops are statistical ties with the fastest rivals.
